originalTitle: Stock Traders Brace For More Volatility After Tech-Driven Rout
summary: Wall Street enters the new trading week under intense pressure after a violent rotation out of US stocks left investors wondering if more pain is in store.
content:
(Bloomberg) -- Wall Street enters the new trading week under intense pressure after a violent rotation out of US stocks left investors wondering if more pain is in store.

Wall Street Asks What Can Save AI Trade After Anthropic Wipeout

H-1B Visa Workers Are Fed Up and Abandoning American Tech Jobs

Yardeni Cuts S&P 500 Target Again, Says Bear Market Is Unlikely

Anthropic CEO Vacations at Italian Resort After Public Listing

California Nvidia Probe Covers Potential Criminal Law Violations

A gauge of expected volatility in the Nasdaq 100 Index is sitting at the highest level since April 2020 after back-to-back punches from the ouster of Jensen Huang from Nvidia Corp. and the Democrats' victory in the midterm elections pushed the tech-heavy index teetering near a bear market. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both entered a correction territory on Friday, defined as a decline of at least 10% from an all-time high.

Futures on the S&P 500 traded up 1.1% at 6:02 pm in New York, while contracts on the Nasdaq 100 added 1.8%. The Cboe Volatility Index, or, VIX, closed above 35 on Friday, its highest level since 2025.

Thinner than normal liquidity into a holiday-shortened week in the US may further amplify volatility in the market already dealing with fundamental risks around the future of the artificial intelligence trade and the Federal Reserve's interest-rate trajectory. Markets are closed on Thursday in observance of the Thanksgiving holiday and will close early on Friday.

"Seasonally, VIX tends to drop in November, particularly with the Thanksgiving holiday," said Amy Wu Silverman, head of derivatives strategy at RBC Capital Markets. "So it's almost comical that VIX is up over 85% so far this month. Unfortunately, it is unlikely that the volatility shock is over given ongoing probes into Nvidia's accounting."

In recent weeks, worries about the sustainability of Wall Street's biggest investment boom in decades had begun to emerge, eroding confidence in the record-setting, AI-fueled rally and the impact of artificial intelligence on growth in the broader economy. At the same time, the scandal engulfing Nvidia, which led to the ouster of Huang following revelations of multiple affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy, has been the single-largest drag on the S&P 500 as it neared a so-called technical correction.

Read: Dip Buyers Hesitate to Step In as Nasdaq 100 Nears a Bear Market

Anthropic PBC shares began trading last week and closed its first session up 17% from its IPO price of $83 per share. However, the Claude chatbot maker's shares ended Friday down 8.5%. The worse-than-expected performance of the highly anticipated initial public offering helped to weigh down the entire equities market.

"While we think it's unlikely that the VIX moves much higher from here, especially into the holidays, we continue to get questions about protecting into yearend as opposed to bottom fishing," said Daniel Kirsch, head of options at Piper Sandler & Co.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc.'s trading desk said last week's selloff has created an attractive opportunity to snap up US stocks. Still, the bank cautions that overall investor positioning remains elevated, signaling the broader capitulation needed for a meaningful rally could be missing.

Hedge funds' equity unwind has become "quite extended" and markets are nearing a "tactical entry" point, the bank's trading desk wrote in a note to clients on Sunday. But a few major headwinds are still in place: the broader stock-market positioning remains elevated, the Federal Reserve is expected to keep raising interest rates and future profits from massive AI investments remain uncertain.
